Definition: from G1722 and πρήθω (to blow a flame); to enkindle, i.e. set on fire:--burn up.
BiblicalUsage: The king in the parable sends his armies, destroys the murderers, and burns up their city in Matthew 22:7 — a picture of judgment carried out to the end.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's judgment is not a threat He forgets — the city that refused the invitation and killed the messengers was burned, and I take that warning seriously.
